name: Red-cockaded Woodpecker
rangeDescription: Patchily distributed in pine forest of southeastern usa
description: Rare and declining woodpecker found exclusively in open pine woodlands. Boldly patterned black and white; note especially prominent white cheek and barred back.

name: Rufous-browed Hemispingus
rangeDescription: Andes of eastern peru (amazonas to la libertad and huánuco)
description: Scarce bird of wet high-elevation forest in the eastern Andes of northern and central Peru. Not often seen, since its remaining habitat is difficult to access.

name: Santa Marta Warbler
rangeDescription: Santa marta mountains (northeastern colombia)
description: Handsome warbler found only at higher elevations in Colombia’s Santa Marta Mountains. The combination of yellow body and ornately patterned black and white head is unique within its limited range.

name: Purple Needletail
rangeDescription: Northern sulawesi and philippines (except palawan)
description: A huge swift of lowlands and mountains, one of the fastest-flying birds in the world. Mainly black with a purplish-blue gloss, an obvious white triangle under the base of the tail, and two pale marks at angles to each other in the center of each wing.

name: Angola Waxbill
rangeDescription: Angola and namibia
description: A tiny colorful seed-eating waxbill with a grayish breast, a yellow belly, an olive-green back finely barred with dark gray, and a scarlet rump and upper tail. The male has a black throat patch that the female lacks.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Moluccan Woodcock
rangeDescription: Northern moluccas (obi and bacan)
description: A chunky, snipe-like forest-dwelling shorebird with cryptic plumage, a stunted tail, and a long powerful bill. Buff below with extensive bold black markings above.

name: Sulu Hornbill
rangeDescription: Sulu archipelago (jolo, tawitawi, and sanga sanga)
description: A large bird of lowland and montane forest on the Sulu Islands, although probably only remaining on Tawi-Tawi. Feeds particularly on fig trees.

name: White-thighed Hornbill
rangeDescription: Humid forest of benin to angola and uganda
description: A large canopy hornbill with a distinct white-tipped tail, a broad white outerwing with white patches within the black forewing, a white belly and vent, and a pale bill. Often seen in the canopy and subcanopy of lowland forest feeding on fruit.

name: Lava Gull
rangeDescription: Galapagos
description: Distinctive gull endemic to Galápagos. Adult is easy to identify by sooty-gray body, black head, white crescents above and below eye, and pale rump.

name: Black-and-white Hawk-Eagle
rangeDescription: Forest of southern mexico to northern argentina and brazil
description: Rare but spectacular eagle of lowland tropical forest. Very rarely seen perched, when black mask, orange-yellow base of bill, and short black crest are distinctive.

name: Restinga Tyrannulet
rangeDescription: Coastal southeastern brazil (southeastern são paulo to northeastern santa catarina)
description: Small olive-green flycatcher with a long slender tail that is often held cocked. Note the yellow eyebrow, yellow throat, and two wingbars.

name: Taiga Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Siberia to kamchatka and northern mongolia; winters to borneo
description: Small brown flycatcher with a sharply contrasting black-and-white tail. Breeding male has an orange throat patch surrounded by a faint gray wash.

name: Red-breasted Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Northern europe to southern urals, balkans, and southern caspian; winters to southern asia
description: Distinctive, small flycatcher. Males have a rusty-orange throat that continues onto the breast.

name: Mentawai Scops-Owl
rangeDescription: Mentawai islands (off western sumatra)
description: This small, dark cinnamon-brown owl is the only resident scops-owl in its limited range. Inhabits a wide range of wooded habitats, from pristine lowland rainforest to plantations and woodlots around human habitation.

name: Black Antbird
rangeDescription: Southern colombia east of andes to northwestern bolivia and southwestern amazonian brazil
description: Long-tailed antbird of lowland rainforest. Most common around tree fall gaps in mature rainforest, and other areas of dense undergrowth.

name: Bougainville Fantail
rangeDescription: Montane forest of bougainville (northwestern solomon islands)
description: Small and drab with a long, often fanned tail. Mostly gray-brown above and slightly lighter tawny below, with a grayish head and a white eyebrow.

name: Striated Lorikeet
rangeDescription: Mountains of western new guinea (snow mountains to chimbu province)
description: A rare, medium-sized lorikeet of foothill and lower montane forest. Green body with yellow-green striations on the face and underparts, and a gray band from the eye around the back of the head.

name: Bronze-tailed Comet
rangeDescription: Pacific slope of andes of peru
description: Large, long-tailed hummingbird found on scrubby slopes in more arid parts of the Peruvian Andes. Adult male is glistening green with an iridescent rosy throat and bronzy tips to the outer tail feathers.

name: Spotted Whistling-Duck
rangeDescription: Sulawesi to new guinea, bismarck archipelago, and southern philippines
description: Small whistling-duck with strongly pale-spotted neck and flanks, dark bill, and gray face. Similar to Wandering Whistling-Duck, but lacks warm rusty coloring, and has pale-spotted rather than dark-spotted breast.

name: Laysan Duck
rangeDescription: Laysan island (northwestern hawaiian islands)
description: Highly range-restricted duck with a splotchy white “comma” around each eye. Found only on the Midway Islands, where it is the only resident duck.
